register.name: Youth Employment Opportunities Project
register.detail: World Bank · IDA · approved 7 July 2026 · executed through the Ministry of Labour, Solidarity and Social Security
register.note: About 22,000 young people aged 16 to 35 to benefit directly, at least half of them women
register.text: A World Bank project to strengthen employment support systems and expand pathways to more and better jobs for young people, with grants for start-ups and small firms and a training centre on Príncipe. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Fiscal Sustainability, Energy Access and Digital Connectivity Development Policy Operation
register.detail: World Bank · IDA grant of SDR 7.3M · approved 7 April 2026 · budget support · first of a series of two
register.note: Prior actions include a decree law on self-generation of renewable energy and a revenue-sharing formula for the electricity sector
register.text: A World Bank budget support grant tied to reforms that strengthen state-owned enterprises and their oversight, improve fiscal transparency, strengthen energy supply and improve digital connectivity. Its rules letting individuals, businesses and communities produce and consume their own renewable energy serve the energy standard.

register.name: Transition Towards Sustainable and Nutritious Food Systems (SIAS)
register.detail: IFAD · grant agreement signed 13 February 2026 · total cost above €15M, co-financed by the Adaptation Fund and the Global Environment Facility · six years
register.note: About 5,500 rural households (around 22,000 people) in 69 communities on São Tomé Island and in the Autonomous Region of Príncipe
register.text: An IFAD grant for climate-resilient farming: rehabilitated irrigation, restored soils and landscapes, agroforestry on 550 hectares and stronger producer organisations, with nutrition education and access to diverse, healthy foods. It serves the food standard, where 54.6% are moderately or severely food insecure.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · originally approved for SDR 18.5M · second review completed 19 December 2025, with a 12-month extension to April 2029 and an augmentation of SDR 4.44M · staff-level agreement on the third review, 22 June 2026
register.note: Disbursements of about US$13.7 million by December 2025; outstanding IMF credit of SDR 31.36 million on 31 March 2026
register.text: An IMF arrangement, now 155 percent of quota, that supports the budget and the balance of payments while the government reforms public finances and the energy sector. The IMF says reforming the energy sector remains essential to unlock growth and ease pressure on public debt and reserves; the floor on pro-poor spending was among the targets met at the second review.

register.name: Social Protection, Resilience and Recovery Project, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank · additional IDA grant of SDR 4.5M · approved 12 September 2025 · closing date extended to 30 June 2028
register.note: Beneficiary households rise from 5,000 to 6,000, about 27,600 people; the monthly transfer of the Vulnerable Family Program rises from 650 to 750 dobras
register.text: Additional World Bank financing for a project that strengthens the social protection system and expands the coverage of its programmes. Cash transfers to poor families serve the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Safeguarding Access to Fiscal and Educational Resources Project (SAFER)
register.detail: World Bank · IDA grant · announced 31 July 2024 · emergency project
register.note: Over 80,000 students and about 4,200 teachers and school administrators
register.text: An emergency World Bank grant that helps the government through a fiscal crisis linked to the energy sector and keeps schools running, including timely pay for teachers and administrators. It also finances energy reforms such as a decarbonisation plan, serving the education and energy standards.

register.name: Coastal Resilience and Sustainable Tourism Project
register.text: Protects the coast and the visitor economy built on it.

register.name: Access to Clean Resilient Electricity (ASCENT)
register.detail: IDA · approved 28 November 2023 · grant agreement of SDR 28.9M signed February 2024 · closes 31 December 2028
register.text: An IDA grant, under the regional ASCENT programme, to increase access to sustainable and clean electricity: solar and battery systems for health and education facilities, off-grid solar home systems for remote households, a utility-scale solar park at Água Casada and last-mile grid connections. It serves the energy standard.
register.note: Includes a solar park at Água Casada, 4 MWh of battery storage and solar home systems for remote households

register.name: Third COVID-19 Recovery and Resilience Development Policy Financing
register.text: Budget support to restore macroeconomic stability.

register.name: Energy Transition, Efficiency, and Expansion Project (ETREEP)
register.detail: African Development Fund · announced 23 April 2026 · $19.02M from ADF-16 and $5.43M from the Transition Support Facility · total investment $30M
register.note: More than 200,000 people and 50,000 households to benefit; 2,000 new connections and over 40,000 prepaid meters
register.text: A grant package for a 4 MWp solar plant with 2 MWh of battery storage on Príncipe, low-voltage network upgrades, 1,000 LED streetlights on São Tomé, a modernised national dispatch centre and green skills training for 200 young people. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Blue Economy and Fisheries Infrastructure Rehabilitation and Maintenance Project (BEFIRM)
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · approved December 2025 · Transition Support Facility Prevention Window and African Development Fund · 2026 to 2030
register.note: 30,000 people along the fish value chain to benefit directly and about 100,000 more indirectly
register.text: A grant to rehabilitate three multipurpose fishing ports, replace aging wooden dugout canoes with 400 climate-resilient fibreglass vessels, refurbish six cold stores and supply four refrigerated trucks. It serves the food and livelihood standards for small-scale fishers, processors and traders.

register.name: Fiscal Sustainability and Economic Resilience Program, supplementary grant
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Nigeria Trust Fund · announced 9 December 2025 · follows a second phase of $7.9M from the Transition Support Facility, announced 31 March 2025
register.note: Total Bank support of about $20 million over two years
register.text: Budget support that closes a financing gap in the 2025 budget, tied to revenue reforms such as VAT and customs modernisation and to energy reforms: utility governance, cost-recovery tariffs, a shift to renewables and prepaid electricity meters. It serves the energy standard and, by the Bank’s account, creates fiscal space for investment in human capital.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2018
items.text: Volcanic peaks, cocoa plantations and beaches on the equator: visitors already earn most of the export income.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Cocoa and coffee plantations: fine harvests that can earn a premium.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 37.5% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

enterprises.heading: Already working in São Tomé and Príncipe.

items.name: CECAQ-11
items.text: A cocoa export cooperative founded in 2009 that unites 1,127 small-scale producers in 21 associations on more than 2,000 hectares, whose organic and fair trade certified cocoa is used in chocolate such as Tierra Madre, and which in June 2026 helped design a cocoa route for visitors in Água Izé.

items.name: Associação dos Produtores de Cacau de Qualidade de Água Izé
items.text: A cocoa producers’ association with more than ten years in the technical and financial management of cocoa production and processing, which since June 2026 runs the Rota do Cacau do Sul, a 2.5 km guided route through its processing centre and members’ plots, with the income shared with local guides.

items.name: CECAB
items.text: The organic cocoa production and export cooperative of smallholder farmers’ associations, which sells to the French chocolate maker Kaoka and whose technical team keeps a field of selected cocoa plants for its members’ farms.

items.name: CECAFEB
items.text: The organic coffee export cooperative at Monte Café, whose values and objectives guide smallholder organic coffee associations such as Nova Riqueza of Água Sampaio.
